samples.question: The cream board is littered with small decorative coloured squares, and exactly one square block of blue WATER sits somewhere on it: that block is the LAGOON. Only what lies inside the lagoon decides the answer; every square on the bare cream board is decoration and means nothing. Inside the lagoon there are exactly three large solid square ISLANDS, each a single colour drawn from red, blue, green and purple, and the three islands have three different colours. Two of the islands each have one LAKE cut into them: a smaller square of the same blue water, completely surrounded by that island's colour. The third island has no lake. The lagoon also carries several small coloured PATCHES, all about the same size as each other. Some patches float directly on the open lagoon water, some are painted on the body of an island, and exactly one patch - the ISLET - lies inside a lake, completely surrounded by water that is itself completely surrounded by an island. So the islet is the only patch you reach by stepping board, lagoon, island, lake, patch. The islet's own colour is always different from the colour of the island that holds its lake, and patch colours, patch sizes, island sizes and island positions carry no other information. What colour is the island whose lake contains the islet? Answer red, blue, green or purple.
